title: Customer Insights - Journeys: Outreach Optimization Agent picks email send times
summary: Hold: the capacity API example omits the environment and allocation body needed to use it, and the quiet-times API omits the Dataverse service version and request body. The briefing also incorrectly treats the underlying Customer Insights licence requirement and compliance-profile quiet-time applicability as unpublished.

claims.claim: Quiet times are configured at Settings > Customer engagement > Quiet times.
claims.quote: To set up quiet times, go to Settings > Customer engagement > Quiet times.

claims.claim: POST /msdynmkt_quiettimesettings is a complete REST call for the quiet-times control.
claims.quote: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/accounts ... Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 ... To create a record, you must identify the valid entity set name, property names, and types.
claims.fix: The cited table reference confirms the entity set and POST operation, but the printed call omits the service version and JSON payload. Replace it with 'POST <organization URL>/api/data/v9.2/msdynmkt_quiettimesettings; Content-Type: application/json; body: <Quiet Time Setting JSON object>'. State in the existing note that this creates a Quiet Time Setting record and requires the caller to supply its configuration. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/create-entity-web-api alongside the existing table reference.

claims.claim: Quiet times can apply for up to 21 consecutive days.
claims.quote: Quiet times can apply for up to 21 consecutive days. ... The combined quiet times effect (both quiet dates and quiet hours) must stay within the 21 day maximum.

claims.claim: The agent honours configured quiet times.
claims.quote: The agent respects your organization's configured quiet times. ... the agent won't schedule emails during quiet-time periods.

claims.claim: The agent honours contact point consent and does not send to an opted-out email address.
claims.quote: The agent respects the communication preferences set for each contact or lead. If a contact has opted out of email communication on a specific address, no email is sent to that address.

claims.claim: Quiet times apply to messages through their compliance profiles.
claims.quote: Once a quiet time has been added to a compliance profile, all messages designated with that compliance profile respect the quiet times configured.

claims.claim: Whether compliance-profile quiet times apply to the agent's messages is not stated.
claims.quote: Once a quiet time has been added to a compliance profile, all messages designated with that compliance profile respect the quiet times configured.
claims.fix: Delete '; Learn's quiet-times page ties them to compliance profiles, and whether the agent reads them the same way is not stated'. Retain 'Check that quiet times are configured in Customer Insights - Journeys and linked to the compliance profile your journey emails use.' The general rule covers these emails, and the agent page explicitly confirms that configured quiet times are honoured.

claims.claim: The printed allocationsV2 PUT with entitlementId and TenantPool rule alone is a usable allocation and overage request.
claims.quote: scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId } ... allocatedEntitlements = @( ... entitlementId = "MCSMessages" ... allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 } ... @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }
claims.fix: The endpoint, PUT method, entitlement and API version are documented; the pre-check's literal-URL miss is caused by variables in the example. Replace the incomplete call with 'PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01; Authorization: Bearer <access token>; Content-Type: application/json; body: {"scope":{"environmentId":"<environment ID>"},"allocatedEntitlements":[{"entitlementId":"MCSMessages","allocation":{"quantity":<credits integer>},"enforcementRules":[{"ruleType":"TenantPool","enabled":false}]}]}'. Add to the existing note: 'This disables tenant-pool draw, not every overage source. An environment-group rule can lock this setting; updates then fail with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.'

claims.quote: If no overage source is enabled, the environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits. Experiences that require credits can stop working after that allocation is exhausted.
